original_value: This paper undertakes a systematic review (SR) on distributed estimation techniques applied to cyber-physical systems (CPS). Even though SRs are not the common way to survey a theme in the control community, they provide a rigorous, robust and objective formula that should not be always ignored. The presented SR incorporates and adapts the guidelines recommended in other fields (mainly biosciences and computer sciences) to the field of automation and control and presents a brief description of the different phases that constitute an SR. As a result, this review compares the different techniques found in the literature in terms of: The proposed estimator (Kalman filter, Luenberger observer, Bayesian filter, etc.), the particular application within CPS, the design of the estimators (decentralized vs centralized), the amount of data required for implementation or the inclusion of experiments/simulations in the studies. Particular attention is paid to those papers that present some results in applications that include humans, animals or biological systems.

result.paraphrase: This paper presents a systematic review (SR) of distributed estimation techniques for cyber-physical systems (CPS). Although SRs are not the usual way to survey a topic in the control community, they offer a rigorous, robust, and objective approach that should not be overlooked. The SR adapts and incorporates guidelines from other fields, mainly biosciences and computer sciences, to automation and control, and briefly describes the phases that make up an SR. The review then compares the literature across several dimensions: the proposed estimator (e.g., Kalman filter, Luenberger observer, Bayesian filter), the specific CPS application, the estimator architecture (centralized versus decentralized), the data needed for implementation, and whether the studies include experiments or simulations. Special emphasis is given to papers reporting results in applications involving humans, animals, or biological systems.
